answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds identities to cryptographic stake burning via an exponential cost curve: registering the $n$-th agent requires burning $\kappa \cdot 2^n$ tokens. Rather than letting rogue nodes echo fabricated votes, attacker expenditure scales superlinearly, driving adversary balances toward an absolute nadir. Meanwhile, legitimate nodes operating under the juniper security protocol preserve decentralized consensus at minimal overhead.
